newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open mostly flat Thursday, trading sources said.

Prices closed barely higher on Wednesday amid refiner buying in the July/October spread, and short-covering in the most-active October contract. Producer selling limited gains and is expected to continue to provide resistance to firmer prices.
Wednesday, spot July ended 0.02 cent firmer at 11.36 cents per lb after trading from 11.41 to 11.29 cents. Most-active October settled up 0.05 cent at 11.31 cents, with the rest 0.02 cent higher.
An estimated 18,221 lots traded hands on the day.
Statistician F.O. Licht today put world sugar output at 123.16 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, down slightly from an earlier estimate. Output reached 125.86 million tonnes last year.

World sugar stocks should reach 48.44 million tonnes raw value by the end of August 1997, representing 40.21 percent of total demand, compared with 39.81 percent last year. The lower figure reflects a drop in Indian consumption, Licht said.

LIFFE spot August white sugar futures were barely higher while the back months stood narrowly mixed, as dealers awaited a sign from the New York market. At 0848 EDT/1248 GMT, August stood $0.60 higher at $323.60, while the back months were trading $0.10 higher to $0.10 lower.
